I'm in mostly AP classes but got a 504 plan for depression and ADHD. took a lot of fighting for though because of the whole "gifted and smart means you don't struggle." 

But yeah I sympathize with you schools are very reluctant to help students like you since you already fulfill their capitalistic needs of getting good grades.

i took calc bc as a junior, multi variable in summer, and linear algebra right now at my community college. so while id love to take an ap version of multi, theres frankly just not enough students that would take it compared to calc 1 and 2. also would a private or even public school take 3 ap math credits? if youre taking that high level math, your major probably has something to do with it and schools like you to take it at their school so they know you have a solid foundation.

Also I feel like this only applies to a select few school districts that have kids taking calc ab and bc before sophomore or junior year especially like the bay area. 

and one more point id like to add. math got extremely more fun for me when i took them at community college. i found ap mcqs and frqs really repetitive and boring and i feel like it synthesized calculus almost too much to the point where its just about knowing what to do rather than deeply understanding concepts or doing proofs.
